unit.title: Energy
unit.blurb: Light, heat, sound and movement – how energy moves, changes, and keeps every living thing going.

O1.t: Know that everything that happens needs energy, and name kinds of energy: light, heat, sound and movement.

O2.t: Know that energy can be transferred, and that batteries, fuels and food store energy.

O3.t: Describe simple energy changes, such as electricity to light, heat, sound or movement.

O4.t: Know that plants use sunlight to make food and that animals get energy by eating; read simple food chains.

captions: Hello, energy explorers!
Everything that happens needs energy.
This is lesson 2.1: energy around us.
Think about your day.
You ran and played. That needs energy.
A lamp gave light. That needs energy too.
A cooker made your food hot. Energy again!
Energy comes in different kinds.
Light energy lets us see.
Heat energy keeps us warm.
Sound energy lets us hear. And movement energy makes things go!
Pause and think.
What kind of energy does a lamp give out?
Look around you. Energy is everywhere!
The Sun gives us light and heat.
A guitar makes sound energy.
A moving car has movement energy. And a battery stores energy until we need it.
Did you know?
Almost all the energy on Earth first came from the Sun. Thank you, Sun!
Riddle time!
I am big and bright. I give the Earth light and heat. What am I?
The Sun!
Your turn.
What kind of energy do you hear when you hit a drum?
Let's go on an energy hunt at home!
Walk around and find things that use energy.
Does it give out light, heat, sound, or movement?
Make a list with pictures.
Let's remember.
Everything that happens needs energy.
Light, heat and sound are kinds of energy.
Moving things have movement energy.
And most of our energy first came from the Sun. Energetic work!

captions: Hello, energy explorers!
Energy can move from one place to another.
This is lesson 2.2: energy transfers.
Imagine you kick a ball.
Your leg is moving. It has movement energy.
When you kick, the energy moves to the ball.
Now the ball moves. Goal! The energy was transferred.
To transfer means to move from one thing to another.
Food gives energy to your body.
Your body gives energy to the ball.
Pause and think.
When you kick a ball, where does the energy go?
Some things store energy, until we need it.
A battery stores energy for a torch or a toy.
Fuels store energy too. Petrol is a fuel for cars. Wood is a fuel for a fire.
And food stores energy for our bodies.
Did you know?
In a torch, energy moves from the battery to the bulb.
Then it comes out as light. Click!
Riddle time!
What runs but never walks, and needs a battery?
A toy car!
Your turn.
Which of these stores energy?
Let's watch energy move in a bouncing ball.
Drop a ball from high up, and watch how high it bounces.
Now drop it from lower down.
Which drop gave the ball more energy?
Let's remember.
Energy can move from one thing to another.
This is called an energy transfer.
Batteries, fuels and food store energy.
And food gives energy to our bodies. Super work!

captions: Hello, energy explorers!
Energy can change from one kind to another.
This is lesson 2.3: energy changes.
Switch on a torch.
The battery has stored energy.
The bulb changes it into light energy.
The light lets us see in the dark!
Many things at home change energy.
A kettle changes electricity into heat, to boil water.
A speaker changes electricity into sound.
A fan changes electricity into movement. Whoosh!
Pause and think.
What does a kettle change electricity into?
Try this now.
Rub your hands together, fast!
Do they feel warm?
The movement energy changed into heat energy.
Did you know?
An old light bulb gets very hot. That wastes energy.
A new LED bulb stays cool and saves energy.
Joke time!
Why did the light bulb do well at school?
Because it was very bright!
Your turn.
What does a fan change electricity into?
Let's find energy changes at home.
Look at things that use electricity, like a lamp or a radio.
What does each one give out? Heat, light, sound or movement?
Draw an arrow to show each change.
Let's remember.
Energy can change from one kind to another.
A bulb changes electricity into light.
A kettle changes electricity into heat.
And rubbing your hands changes movement into heat. Brilliant work!

q.prompt: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, which animal eats the rabbit?

twin.prompt: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, what does the rabbit eat?

captions: Hello, nature explorers!
Where do plants and animals get their energy?
This is lesson 2.4: energy and living things.
Plants do not eat like we do.
Plants use energy from sunlight.
They make their own food in their leaves.
Plants are called producers, because they produce food.
Animals cannot make their own food.
A rabbit eats grass. It gets energy from the grass.
A fox eats the rabbit, and gets energy from the rabbit.
This is a food chain. Animals are called consumers, because they eat.
Pause and think.
Where does a plant get its energy from?
You are in a food chain too!
Sunlight helps wheat to grow.
The wheat is made into bread.
You eat the bread, and get energy to play!
Did you know?
An elephant spends most of the day eating grass and leaves.
It needs lots of energy for its huge body!
Riddle time!
What comes first in every food chain?
A plant! It uses energy from the Sun.
Your turn.
In the food chain grass, rabbit, fox, which animal eats the rabbit?
Let's make your own food chain.
Draw a plant first.
Next, draw an animal that eats the plant. Then an animal that eats that animal.
Join them with arrows to show where the energy goes.
Let's remember.
Plants use energy from sunlight to make their own food.
Plants are producers.
Animals eat plants or other animals to get energy. They are consumers.
And a food chain shows who eats what. Wild work!
